chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام informed me, saying: “The deceased is begun with at his private part, then he is given wudu (ablution) like the wudu of salat (prayer).” And he mentioned the hadith.

key_terms.الْحَدِيثَ: the narration being cited in abbreviated form
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person being prepared after death
key_terms.بِفَرْجِهِ: with his private part; i.e. beginning with cleansing that area
key_terms.وُضُوءَ الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual ablution performed in the manner of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be ritually purified according to this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith states part of the prescribed procedure for preparing the deceased, beginning with cleansing the private area and then performing wudu (ablution) as for salat (prayer). It belongs to the jurisprudence of funerary purification and indicates an ordered ritual process in handling the dead.
